The tiger (Panthera tigris) is the largest living cat species, recognised by its powerful body, sharp claws, muscular limbs, and distinctive orange coat covered in black stripes. Tigers are skilled hunters with exceptional night vision, strong jaws, and the ability to move quietly through dense vegetation. Unlike most cats, they are also excellent swimmers and often use rivers and lakes to cool down or travel. Tigers symbolise strength, courage, independence, and raw power. They inhabit forests, grasslands, mangroves, and other environments across parts of Asia. Unlike lions, tigers are generally solitary animals, patrolling large territories and hunting prey such as deer and wild boar. Despite their strength, they face serious threats from habitat loss, poaching, and conflicts with humans. Fun fact: Every tiger has a unique pattern of stripes, and the markings extend onto its skin beneath the fur. No two tigers have exactly the same stripe pattern.  #Tiger #PantheraTigris #Wildlife #BigCats #Nature

Seven tigers removed from tiny cages in Circo Rey Gitano in Guatemala are in an ADI Temporary Rescue Unit (ADI TRU) while preparations are made to take them to a new life at the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary. This is a temporary hospital facility where the cages used to remove the tigers from the circus are joined together to give the animals more space.  Already the tigers have more space than they had in the circus and in some cases, more than three times the space. The animals can be separated for feeding, veterinary treatment and for cage cleaning – a cage is being cleaned in the background. We will soon be adding exercise enclosures with small pools.  The ADI Wildlife Sanctuary in South Africa will be their forever home with huge natural enclosures  – each tiger will have at least 10,000 square meters / 107,639 square feet. All seven tigers were successfully removed from the circus by Guatemala’s animal welfare division, Unidad de Bienestar Animal (UBA) and wildlife department Consejo Nacional de Areas Protegidas (CONAP) and police.  All are well at the ADI TRU and this has been verified by officials and the Guatemala media. These tigers deserve some freedom for their final years, don’t let them be forced back into the tiny circus cages they have endured for years. Speak up for the tigers. #StopCircusSuffering
